title: Gray Code Sequence
description: An `n`-bit Gray code sequence is an ordering of all `2^n` integers in `[0, 2^n - 1]` starting with `0` where consecutive elements (as well as the first and last elements) differ in exactly one binary bit. Given `n`, return the standard reflected binary Gray code sequence defined by `seq[i] = i ^ (i >> 1)` for `0 <= i < 2^n`.
hints: Each index `i` maps directly to its reflected binary Gray code via `i ^ (i >> 1)`.
Verify that `i` and `i + 1` differ by a trailing run of `1`s flipping to `0`s plus one carry bit, so `(i ^ (i >> 1))` and `((i + 1) ^ ((i + 1) >> 1))` differ in exactly one bit.

examples.explanation: For n = 3, the 8-element reflected binary Gray code is [0, 1, 3, 2, 6, 7, 5, 4].
